subject: Re: Post-call recap & SLO clarifications - latency/throughput/SLAs
messages:

Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - performance/SLO items

Hi John - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the follow-ups I promised: 

- Primary performance targets you mentioned: p95 latency <= 200ms for chat/generation at 256-token responses, sustained throughput of ~500 requests/min, and concurrent user sessions of ~200. You also called out streaming support for token-by-token playback in the UI.
- Open questions we agreed to clarify: how you want latency measured (end-to-end vs server-only), acceptable maintenance/exclusion windows, and reporting cadence for SLIs/SLOs.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) I'll send a written proposal of how we measure latency (p50/p95/p99 definitions, server-side vs end-to-end) and proposed SLA language for exclusions and remedies.
2) We'll include a performance appendix (sample throughput tests for 256/1024 token responses, concurrency assumptions).
3) Rishi will schedule a brief engineering sync if we need to validate streaming handshake/partial-response behavior with your front-end.

Can you confirm the numbers above reflect your internal targets and whether you want strict end-to-end (client + network) SLOs or server-side? If end-to-end, do you have preferred monitoring endpoints?

Best,
Marissa
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>

Date: 2026-11-18T12:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - performance/SLO items

Thanks Marissa - yes, those targets are accurate. A few clarifications: 

- For UI-level SLAs we prefer end-to-end p95 (what our users experience), but we understand server-side measurement is more tractable for provider SLAs. We're open to a hybrid approach (server-side SLOs + guidance for network/client variance).
- Streaming: we need token-by-token streaming with per-token latency (time from model token emitted to delivery to client) for live playbacks. Also want bounded tail latency for the initial token - ideally p95 <= 150ms for first token.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows are fine; how do you treat cold-starts after scale-ups or model swaps? Those will cause spikes.

If you can share proposed SLA language covering measurement definitions, exclusions (maintenance, force majeure, network third-party), reporting cadence, and remedies (credits tiers), that would help us move forward.

John
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp
john.doe@acme.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - performance/SLO items

John - appreciate the clarity. Attached is a draft SLA (Redwood_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf) and a short performance appendix. Below are the key points pulled into email form so you have them immediately: 

1) Measurement definitions
- Request: a single API call that initiates generation or streaming. For streaming we treat the request lifecycle as: initial response latency (time to first byte/token) and token emission latency (inter-token intervals).
- Latency metrics reported: p50, p95, p99 for initial response (time from request arrival at Redwood ingress to first byte sent), and p50/p95 for per-token emission during streaming.
- Throughput: measured as sustained successful requests/minute at target payload sizes (we'll show sample curves for 256 and 1024-token responses in the appendix).
- Concurrency: measured as number of concurrent active model sessions handled by a reserved worker pool.

2) Server-side vs end-to-end
- Our standard SLA measures server-side latency (Redwood ingress -> first byte emitted from our runtime). We provide guidance and sample client-side benchmarking to estimate network contribution.
- Hybrid option: Redwood will report server-side SLOs in the contract and provide a recommended margin (e.g., add 30-50ms for typical network variance). If Acme requires user-facing (end-to-end) SLOs, we can include a joint monitoring plan (synthetics from your edge locations) and define shared indicators in the contract.

3) Exclusions and edge cases
- Scheduled maintenance windows: excluded (we propose monthly maintenance < 2 hours, plus pre-notice).
- Force majeure, third-party network outages, customer-side misconfigurations: excluded.
- Cold-starts after autoscale/model swap: we propose an exclusion window for immediate scale events (first 2 minutes after up-scaling events) unless a priority warm pool is negotiated.
- Misuse/flooding/traffic outside agreed rate limits: excluded.

4) Reporting cadence and transparency
- Monthly SLI report with p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, error rates, and concurrency distribution.
- Real-time dashboard access for agreed metrics; logs/trace exports available via secure link on request.
- For incidents affecting SLOs, we provide a post-incident report within 72 hours with root cause analysis.

5) Remedies and credits
- Service credits tied to monthly uptime and latency adherence. Examples (negotiable):
  - p95 breach <= 5% of monthly requests: 10% credit on monthly invoice
  - p95 breach between 5%–15%: 25% credit
  - p95 breach > 15%: 50% credit + contract review
- Credits are exclusive of other remedies; SLAs will carve out cases where credits do not apply (see exclusions).

6) Streaming specifics
- Initial token (first byte) SLO: suggested p95 <= 150ms for first token for streaming endpoints - we can include this as a negotiated addendum.
- Per-token emission SLOs measured as p95 of inter-token latency across streaming sessions.
- We support chunked response formats and event-streaming; can provide a short integration test we run jointly to validate real-world playback under your CDN topology.

If this looks good I'll circulate a small redlineable PDF (attached) that you can share with procurement. If you want end-to-end SLOs we'll need to align on synthetic monitoring locations and define the joint measurement plan.

Next steps we propose:
- You and procurement review the attached SLA draft and mark redlines.
- Rishi to set up a 30-min engineering sync on streaming behavior and concurrency assumptions (I'll propose times).
- We'll run a joint perf test (sample appendix) to validate the throughput/concurrency curves.

Happy to jump on a quick call if any of the bullets need faster resolution.

Best,
Marissa
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf (draft SLA), acme_performance_appendix.xlsx (sample perf curves)
